project.objective: Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas of Funchal, Madeira have a wife named Antonia de Jesus, distinct from his tree-recorded wife Maria Joana (m. 1890), and a daughter named Maria who died young?

questions.question: Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas of Funchal, Madeira marry a woman named Antonia de Jesus prior to or in addition to his recorded marriage to Maria Joana (ca. 1890)?
questions.rationale: The research objective requires establishing whether a prior or additional spousal relationship existed for Antonio Fernandes Lucas. Funchal Catholic parish marriage registers survive and are available on FamilySearch for this period, making the question testable. Confirming or disconfirming the Antonia de Jesus marriage is the gatekeeper for the second part of the objective — the daughter Maria question — because a baptism record for Maria would likely name her mother, linking the two facts. Starting with the marriage question also anchors chronology: if Antonia de Jesus preceded Maria Joana (m. ca. 1890), the records searched will be pre-1890 Funchal parish registers.

exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: Two independent positive records confirm GK89-82B's only marriage; two additional records provide cross-corroborated negative evidence establishing the Antonia de Jesus connection belongs to a different family branch. Full-text and external searches (pli_004, pli_006) were skipped as the recovered evidence is sufficient without ambiguity.
exhaustive_declaration.justification: Searched FamilySearch collections 4426199 (Catholic Church Records) and 4474701 (Civil Records) for Funchal/Madeira with multiple queries. Recovered 4 records bearing on q_001. The conclusion (GK89-82B did NOT marry Antonia de Jesus) is supported by two independent records of his actual 1890 marriage AND by two independent records explicitly placing the Antonia de Jesus connection in the collateral Manoel branch. No further indexed record search is expected to yield new evidence material to the question.

questions.question: Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B, b. ca. 1838, Santo António, Funchal, Madeira) have a daughter named Maria who died young?
questions.rationale: The second part of the research objective asks whether GK89-82B had a daughter named Maria who died young. The baptism-as-father search (pli_003, log_002) surfaced 'Maria Fernandes Lucas' christenings in Santo António in 1873, 1874, 1886, and 1892 within a broad result pool for fathers named 'Antonio' — these candidates need evaluation to determine which, if any, belong to GK89-82B. A daughter who died young implies both a baptism record and a burial/death record may exist. The question depends on q_001 having established GK89-82B's only documented marriage (Maria Joana, 1890): any daughter pre-1890 would have been born outside that marriage.

exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: Three search vectors exhausted: Catholic baptisms, Catholic deaths, civil deaths — all returning Manoel-branch records (mother=Antonia de Jesus or grandfather=Manuel Fernandes Lucas). No evidence of a daughter Maria born to GK89-82B + Maria Joana found in any indexed source. Image review skipped as indexed evidence is conclusive.
exhaustive_declaration.justification: The searches are reasonably exhaustive per GPS Element 1: baptism and death registers were searched in both church and civil collections; multiple name-variant strategies were applied; all candidates examined showed mother=Antonia de Jesus (not Maria Joana). The absence of any Maria with mother=Maria Joana across three independent record sources constitutes adequate negative evidence.

items.rationale: Collection 4426199 (Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990) is the primary repository for all Funchal parish marriage registers: 1.3M indexed records, 17.7M person profiles, 604K images. Searching for Antonio Fernandes Lucas as groom should surface every recorded marriage across all Funchal parishes. Portuguese Catholic marriage registers name both parties, their parents, witnesses, and date. The 1860-1895 window covers any pre-1890 marriage to Antonia de Jesus and the ca. 1890 marriage to Maria Joana for cross-verification. Locality guide loc_001 confirms this collection is searchable by name (85-99% indexed in most parish volumes).

Collection 1520605 (Portugal Marriages, 1670-1910) is a national index (45,182 records) that may surface records not captured in the Madeira-specific collection, or confirm a find from item 1 with a second indexed entry. Fallback if item 1 yields no marriage to Antonia de Jesus, or used to verify any positive hit. Searching on FamilySearch is free and fast.

Catholic baptism registers in Madeira name the child's father AND mother in every entry. Searching collection 4426199 for Antonio Fernandes Lucas as father across all Funchal parishes 1860-1900 will reveal which women bore children with him and when: if Antonia de Jesus appears as mother in baptisms before ca. 1890 and Maria Joana appears after, this constitutes strong indirect evidence of two distinct relationships. Godparent names in these same records often identify close relatives and FAN-cluster associates who may appear in other record types. Covers both q_001 (Antonia de Jesus as wife) and the related daughter-Maria question. Santo António, São Gonçalo, and São Pedro parish volumes 1860-1899 are confirmed digitized and 85-99% name-indexed per loc_001 volume survey.

Several Santo António batismos volumes from 1860-1869 are confirmed 0% name-indexed and not reachable by record_search (loc_001). A full-text co-occurrence search via the search-full-text skill — searching 'Lucas' + 'Antonia' (or 'Fernandes' + 'Antonia') across the unindexed Madeira corpus — will surface any page where both terms appear together, including marriage banns, baptism entries, and burial records that indexed search cannot reach. This is particularly important for the 1860-1878 pre-civil-registration window. Route this item to the search-full-text skill, not record_search.

Portuguese civil registration began in 1878. Collection 4474701 (Portugal, Civil Records, 1437-2023) covers civil marriage registers post-1878. The ca. 1890 marriage to Maria Joana should appear here if conducted civilly. Searching Antonio Fernandes Lucas in civil marriage records verifies the tree-recorded Maria Joana marriage and may surface an earlier or additional civil marriage to Antonia de Jesus (possible if any marriage occurred after 1878). Civil marriage records name both parties and their parents, supplying full identification. This also independently verifies or challenges the 'ca. 1890' date in the tree, which is currently unsourced.

Tombo.pt (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) and the Madeira Regional Archive online catalog (biblioteca.abm.madeira.gov.pt) provide access to Madeira civil and church records not indexed on FamilySearch, and support name-based searching. Searching Antonio Fernandes Lucas at these portals cross-checks FamilySearch findings and may surface additional marriage or baptism records, particularly for post-1878 civil records where FamilySearch coverage of Madeira may be incomplete. Route to search-external-sites skill.

Search FamilySearch collection 4426199 (Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records) for baptism of a child named Maria with father Antonio Fernandes Lucas. The pli_003 broad search (log_002) already returned 'Maria Fernandes Lucas' christening candidates for 1873, 1874, 1886, and 1892 within a large result pool. This plan item runs a targeted search: givenName=Maria, fatherSurname=Lucas, fatherGivenName=Antonio, in Santo António / Funchal. The goal is to identify which 'Maria Fernandes Lucas' children (if any) have father 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas' matching GK89-82B's profile (José branch, born ~1838), as opposed to the Manoel-branch namesake (I3, I8).

Search FamilySearch collection 4426199 for burial/death records of a child named Maria Fernandes Lucas. A daughter who 'died young' should have a burial entry in the same Catholic parish registers. Searching by surname=Lucas, givenName=Maria, recordType=death, in Santo António / Funchal, should surface any Maria who died in childhood. If a burial record is found and the listed parents include Antonio Fernandes Lucas (José branch), that would directly answer q_002 YES.

Search FamilySearch collection 4474701 (Portugal, Civil Records) for a civil death record for Maria Fernandes Lucas in Funchal. Civil registration began in Madeira in 1878; a child dying after 1878 should have both a church burial and a civil death registration. Civil death records name the parents, which would confirm which Antonio Fernandes Lucas was the father. Fallback from the church burial search (pli_008).

If the targeted baptism search (pli_007) and burial searches (pli_008, pli_009) yield candidates that cannot be attributed to GK89-82B vs. the namesake through indexed fields alone, read the original baptism register image (ark:/61903/1:2:H92K-X1N6 and adjacent entries per volume_search) to check the father's patronymic or any marginal notation. Image review may also resolve h_001 (the paternal-grandfather identity in the 1890 baptism record). Fallback if indexed attribution is ambiguous.

This is a DIFFERENT person: our subject GK89-82B has father José Fernandes Lucas (not Manoel). The 1859 Antonia de Jesus marriage belongs to the Manoel branch of the Lucas family. This is direct negative evidence that GK89-82B did NOT marry Antonia de Jesus.

## Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) marry Antonia de Jesus?

**Conclusion: Probably not.** Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B, b. 22 Apr 1838, Santo António, Funchal, Madeira) has one documented marriage: to Maria Joana on 8 February 1890 in Santo António, Funchal. No record connects him to any woman named Antonia de Jesus. One open identity thread prevents a 'proved' tier (see h_001).

### GPS Element 1 — Reasonably Exhaustive Research

Two FamilySearch collections covering Madeiran records for the target period were searched with multiple query variants (pli_001 and pli_005 for marriages; pli_003 for baptisms as father). Nine log entries document the search process. Four records bearing on the question were extracted. Planned full-text (pli_004) and external searches (pli_006) were skipped as current evidence is sufficient to reach a probable negative conclusion; executing them could upgrade the tier to 'proved.' The original image for 6NGD-3SZ7 (ark:/61903/1:2:H92K-X1N6) has not been read — doing so is the primary path to resolving h_001.

### GPS Element 2 — Evidence Analysis

**Two independent records confirm GK89-82B's sole marriage:**
- *Catholic church record 6BG7-FC2X (src_001):* Groom Antonio Fernandes Lucas, father José Fernandes Lucas, mother Francisca Luisa da Conceicao, marries Maria Joanna de Jesus (b. 1869, parents Antonio de Nóbrega + Luisa de Jesus) on 8 Feb 1890, Santo António. `same_person` score vs. GK89-82B: 0.895 (strong). *Original/primary/direct.*
- *Civil registration X91Y-HHF4 (src_002):* Same groom, same parents, same date and place. Bride indexed as 'Antonio de Jesus' (gender=Female); five corroborating attributes identify her as the same Maria Joana from src_001. *Original/primary/direct.*

These records were created by different registrars and constitute independent evidentiary units that agree on every material fact.

**Negative evidence points away from an Antonia de Jesus connection:**
- *Catholic church record 6BG7-MQ3D (src_003):* A namesake groom (I3) married Antonia de Jesus (I6) on 20 July 1859. His father is **Manoel** Fernandes Lucas (a_054), not GK89-82B's father **José** (a_005, a_029). Two different fathers = two different men. *Original/primary/direct. Evidence type: negative.*
- *Baptismal record 6NGD-3SZ7 (src_004):* A child born 18 July 1890 has mother 'Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas' (I9), whose maternal grandparents are Manoel Fernandes Lucas + Luiza de Jesus (a_080, a_084) — the Manoel-branch parents. This places I9 firmly in the Manoel branch. The father in this record (I8) is also named 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas'; his own parentage has not been independently confirmed (see h_001 and a_087). *Original/primary/direct. Evidence type: negative (for I9's branch), indeterminate (for I8's identity).*

### Open Thread — h_001

The 1890 baptism uses the mother's (I9's) Manoel-branch parentage to link the 'Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas' in that record to the collateral family. However, the identity of the FATHER (I8, also 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas') is not directly confirmed as belonging to the Manoel branch rather than to GK89-82B's José branch. The paternal-grandfather entry in the index (a_087) appeared from an adjacent register entry and was flagged for original-image confirmation. This open thread, combined with a_094's own acknowledgement that 'a separate Antonia de Jesus from José's branch may exist but has not been found,' prevents escalation to 'proved.' Hypothesis h_001 documents the specific question.

**Upgrade path:** Read the original register image (ark:/61903/1:2:H92K-X1N6) to confirm the paternal_grandfather's name. If the grandfather is Manoel Fernandes Lucas (= I4), h_001 can be confirmed and ps_001 upgraded to 'proved.'

### GPS Element 3 — Correlation and Analysis

The father-name conflict between the 1859 marriage record and GK89-82B's established parentage is independently corroborated by the 1890 baptismal record's maternal-grandparent naming. Two records from different years, different event types, and different registrations converge on the Manoel branch for the 'Antonia de Jesus' connection. A birth-year conflict (tree: 1838 vs. marriage records: approximate 1839) was resolved in favour of the christening record as the contemporaneous primary source (c_001). This conflict has no bearing on the marriage question.

### GPS Element 4 — Soundly Reasoned, Written Conclusion

The preponderance of direct and negative evidence supports the conclusion that Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) never married Antonia de Jesus. His only documented marriage is to Maria Joana, 8 February 1890. The appearance of an 'Antonia de Jesus' connection in Santo António records is explained by the collateral Manoel-branch Lucas family. One image review (h_001) is required to upgrade from probable to proved.

## Q_002: Did GK89-82B have a daughter named Maria who died young?

### Conclusion: Probably not.

Five independent records in three record types — Catholic church baptisms, Catholic church deaths, and civil death registration — all returned the same finding: every candidate 'Maria Fernandes Lucas' who died young in Santo António, Funchal is a child of the **Manoel branch** of the family, not of GK89-82B.

### Evidence

**1. Baptism of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 11 Oct 1886 (6NG6-XHM2, src_006 / a_111, a_116):**
The baptism register names the child's father as Antonio Fernandes Lucas and records her paternal grandfather as **Manuel Fernandes Lucas** (paternal grandmother: Luiza de Jesus). GK89-82B's documented father was **José** Fernandes Lucas — not Manuel. This is the single most diagnostic piece of evidence: the grandfather's name places this child unambiguously in the Manoel branch, entirely independently of the mother-name comparison.

**2. Catholic church death of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 30 May 1889 (6B2L-FKDG, src_005 / a_098, a_100):**
The death register names father Antonio Fernandes Lucas and mother **Antonia de Jesus**. GK89-82B's only documented wife is **Maria Joana de Jesus** (married 8 Feb 1890). 'Antonia de Jesus' is the wife of the Manoel-branch Antonio Fernandes Lucas — a different woman from a different family branch. The mother's name directly excludes GK89-82B from this child's parentage.

Note also the timeline: Maria was born in September 1886 and died in May 1889 — nine months *before* GK89-82B married Maria Joana on 8 February 1890. A child born and dying before GK89-82B's only documented marriage cannot be a daughter of that union.

**3. Civil registration death of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 30 May 1889 (6YPM-36RZ, src_007 / a_132, a_137):**
The civil registrar's record is independent of the Catholic church register (different authority, different officiant). It lists the same child, the same death date, and the same parents: father Antonio Fernandes Lucas, mother **Antonia de Jesus**. Two independent record sources — church and civil — converge on the same exclusion. This independence strengthens the attribution to the Manoel branch beyond what a single source could provide.

**4. Catholic church death of Maria Lucas, 5 Sep 1894 (6BCT-KZMJ, src_008 / a_143, a_144):**
This record addresses the post-marriage window directly. Maria Lucas was born in 1893 — three years after GK89-82B's marriage to Maria Joana in February 1890. A daughter born during the GK89-82B–Maria Joana marriage would fall exactly into this period. Yet the death register names this child's mother as **Antonia de Jesus** — not Maria Joana. Born in 1893, dying 5 September 1894, in Santo António: this is a second Manoel-branch daughter named Maria, showing that the pattern extends into the post-1890 period. No record with mother=Maria Joana de Jesus and daughter=Maria was found in any searched collection, even in the years after their marriage.

**5. Baptism of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 26 Dec 1892 (6NR2-ZMW7, src_009 / a_158, a_160):**
This record reveals the depth of the Manoel-branch family network in Santo António. The 1892 Maria's father is Antonio Fernandes Lucas (a Manoel-branch son), and her mother is **d'Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas** — a woman who is herself a daughter of the Manoel-branch couple (Antonio Fernandes Lucas + Antonia de Jesus = I8 + I6). The name 'Antonia de Jesus' thus appears not only as a wife but as a maternal grandmother, and the inherited surname 'Fernandes Lucas' on the mother confirms her branch membership without ambiguity. This third-generation record demonstrates that all reachable 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas + daughter Maria' baptisms in Santo António trace through the Manoel-branch family network.

### Evidence synthesis

Five candidate records were examined across baptism and death registers (church and civil). The records span 1886–1894 and include both the pre-marriage and post-marriage periods relative to GK89-82B's February 1890 union with Maria Joana. All five records identify either (a) Antonia de Jesus as the child's mother, (b) Manuel Fernandes Lucas as the child's paternal grandfather, or (c) Antonia de Jesus as the child's maternal grandmother. None names Maria Joana de Jesus as a mother. The three naming mechanisms are independent — no single analytical step connects all five records — and they converge on the same conclusion: the entire indexed population of 'Maria Fernandes Lucas died young in Santo António' belongs to the Manoel branch, not to GK89-82B.

### Open threads

- **Unindexed records**: the exhaustive declaration covers indexed sources only. Records not yet transcribed into the FamilySearch name index could theoretically contain a daughter Maria of GK89-82B + Maria Joana. No positive evidence for this exists.
- **h_001 (I8 identity)**: the identity of the Manoel-branch father (I8) as a distinct person from GK89-82B was not independently confirmed by image review. However, the q_002 conclusion does not depend on I8's identity: record 1 above (6NG6-XHM2, a_116) proves the Manoel-branch attribution through the grandfather's name alone, without reference to I8's individual identity.

### GPS assessment

The conclusion rests on three types of negative evidence — mother's name (four records), grandfather's name (one baptism), and an independent civil registration — spanning pre-marriage and post-marriage periods, from three separate record types, with person-evidence linking establishing that the named mothers and grandfathers are identified Manoel-branch persons (I6, I8, I4). The conclusion is rated **probable** rather than proved because absence of positive evidence in indexed records does not preclude the existence of unindexed records naming Maria Joana as the mother. The preponderance of available evidence supports the conclusion that GK89-82B did not have a daughter named Maria who died young.

# Locality Guide: Funchal, Madeira, Portugal (1860–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Funchal city chartered ca. 1508; the Distrito de Funchal (covering all of Madeira) dates from 1420, restructured as "Madeira" region in 1976.
- **Administrative center:** Funchal (island capital)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Portugal; diocesan authority under the Diocese of Funchal (Bispado do Funchal), established 1514.
- **Economy:** Sugar, wine (Madeira wine), embroidery, fishing. Significant emigration to Brazil and Hawaii during this period.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic; small Anglican/Protestant community (British residents).
- **Key historical events:** Major emigration waves to Brazil, Hawaii (1878–1911), and the US.

## Boundary changes
- No significant boundary changes affecting record jurisdiction within 1860–1900. All of Madeira comprised the *Distrito de Funchal* under historical standardPlace "Funchal, Portugal" (+1420/+1976). After 1976 renamed "Madeira, Portugal."
- Records created before 1976 are filed under the historical jurisdiction; both standardPlace forms retrieve the same records on FamilySearch.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Portuguese civil registration commenced nationally in 1878 (Código de Registo Civil).
- **Where held:** Madeira Regional Archive (abm.madeira.gov.pt) holds originals. FamilySearch collection 4426199 covers Madeira records.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers are the primary source before 1878 and remain important through the 1880s–1890s.

### Church records
- **Primary FamilySearch collection:** "Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990" (collection 4426199) — 1,329,527 indexed records, 17,724,331 person profiles, 604,364 images.
- **Confirmed digitized parishes (1860–1900):** Santo António (baptisms + deaths 1860-1899, 85-99% indexed); São Gonçalo (baptisms 1870-1890, 81-96% indexed); São Pedro (deaths 1860-1874 confirmed). Additional parishes on further volume_search pages.
- **Language:** Portuguese (some Latin in older registers).
- **Access:** Name-searchable on FamilySearch (coll. 4426199); also indexed on FindMyPast and MyHeritage.

### Census records
- Portuguese national censuses: 1864, 1878, 1890, 1900. Not indexed online; held at ANTT and ABM.
- Róis de Confessados (annual parish household lists) available via ANTT — useful census substitute.

### Probate and court records
- Held at Madeira Regional Archive and ANTT; not systematically digitized for FamilySearch.

### Passport records
- "Portugal, Madeira Passports 1872-1910" on Ancestry and at abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/.
- FamilySearch volume for Funchal passport applications 1859–1863 (0% name-indexed, full-text searchable only).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Portugal, Madeira Catholic Church Records 1044-1990 (4426199); national Baptisms/Marriages/Deaths indexes | Free |
| Tombo.pt | tombo.pt/en/d/madeira — Madeira civil reg, church records, passports | Free |
| Ancestry | Portugal Select Baptisms/Marriages/Deaths; Madeira Passports 1872-1910 | Subscription |
| FindMyPast | Portugal Baptism/Marriage/Death Indexes 1570-1910 | Subscription |
| Madeira Regional Archive | abm.madeira.gov.pt — online passport search and catalog | Free |

## Records NOT online
- Portuguese national census records (1864, 1878, 1890, 1900) — held at ANTT and ABM.
- Róis de Confessados — partial via ANTT; not indexed on FamilySearch.
- Notarial records (escrituras, testamentos) — physical at ABM.

## Research tips
- Identify the correct parish first; search national Madeira collection (4426199) by name, then drill into parish volumes.
- 'de Jesus' is a very common Marian surname for women in 19th-century Madeira — distinguish by parents' names, age, and parish.
- After 1878, search both parish and civil registers.
- Baptism records name both parents — the key evidence for identifying a child's mother.
- Tombo.pt and the ABM online catalog are important cross-checks alongside FamilySearch.
